title: Management groups: organising subscriptions for governance at scale
learningObjective: Plan and build a management group tree. Move subscriptions safely. Predict which Policy and RBAC rules apply after a move.

prerequisites.text: Management groups and the scope hierarchy (AZ-900)

foundation: A management group is a folder for subscriptions. You put subscriptions (and other management groups) inside it, and whatever rules or permissions you set on the folder apply to everything inside.
Every tenant has one top folder called the Tenant Root Group. You build a tree below it, for example Platform, Landing zones → Prod and Dev, and Sandbox.
Moving a subscription from one folder to another changes which rules apply to it straight away.
engineer: Tree rules: one root management group per tenant (its ID is the tenant ID); up to six levels below the root (the root and subscriptions don't count); up to 10,000 management groups per directory; every management group and subscription has exactly one parent.

What passes down: Policy and RBAC assignments on a management group apply to everything below it: child management groups, subscriptions, resource groups and resources. You can also create budgets on a management group.
Where new subscriptions go: into the root, unless you set a default management group in Hierarchy settings.
Who can create management groups: by default, any user in the tenant. Turn on 'Require write permissions for creating new management groups' to stop that.

Moving a subscription needs: Owner on the subscription; management group write (Owner, Contributor or Management Group Contributor) on the new parent; the same on the current parent, unless the current parent is the root.
What can't change: the root can't be moved or deleted. A management group can only be deleted when it's empty. Its ID can't change, but its display name can.
Global Administrators: they have no Azure access to the root by default. They can elevate (User Access Administrator at /), give the right roles, then turn elevation off.

animation.caption: Move subscriptions between management groups, watch inheritance change, and hit the depth limit.

example.title: Moving an app from sandbox to production
body: sub-app1 starts under Sandbox. There, developers have Contributor and a budget caps spending. When the app goes live, the platform team moves sub-app1 under Landing zones → Prod.

At once, the Sandbox Contributor role stops applying, and the Prod rules 'Require costCenter tag' and 'Deny public IPs' start applying. Existing public IPs aren't deleted; they show as non-compliant. That's why the team checks compliance before the move.

prerequisites: A planned tree (often based on Cloud Adoption Framework landing zones)
Access at the root or the management groups involved
permissions: Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/write (Owner, Contributor or Management Group Contributor) on the parent management groups
Owner on a subscription, to move it
Write access on the root management group, to change Hierarchy settings
limits: One parent per management group or subscription
portal: Search 'Management groups' > Create: enter the management group ID (immutable) and display name.
Open a management group > Add management group / Add subscription, or select a subscription > Move.
Management groups > Settings (root): set the default management group for new subscriptions and require write permissions for creating management groups.
Open any management group > Access control (IAM) or Policy to assign roles and policies that inherit downward.
configuration.cli:
az account management-group create --name mg-prod --display-name "Prod" --parent mg-landingzones
az account management-group subscription add --name mg-prod --subscription <subscription-id>
az account management-group show --name mg-landingzones --expand --recurse
az account management-group update --name mg-prod --display-name "Production"

lab.objective: Move a subscription with the right permissions, explain the inheritance change, and find the depth limit.
steps: Select sub-app1 and target Prod. Try to move it without 'MG write on current parent' and read the error.
Tick the missing permission and move it. Compare the inherited assignments before and after.
Create child management groups under Prod repeatedly until creation fails at the depth limit.
expected: The move fails without write on the current parent (Sandbox)
After the move, Sandbox's Contributor assignment no longer applies and Prod's policies do

validation.text: Moved a subscription to a different management group

failureScenarios: Missing permission on the current parent
Trying to create a seventh level
Expecting existing non-compliant resources to be removed after the move
lab.cost: None. Management groups are free; the simulation runs in the browser.

troubleshooting.cause: You're missing Owner on the subscription, or management group write on the old or new parent.
troubleshooting.fix: Check Access control (IAM) on all three. Management Group Contributor gives management group write.

troubleshooting.symptom: You can't delete a management group.
troubleshooting.cause: It still has management groups or subscriptions inside.

troubleshooting.symptom: A Global Administrator can't see management groups.
troubleshooting.cause: Entra roles don't give Azure access.
troubleshooting.fix: Elevate for a short time, give an Azure role on the root management group, then turn elevation off.

troubleshooting.cause: They land in the root, or in a default management group with no policies.
troubleshooting.fix: In Hierarchy settings, set the default management group to one with rules (for example Sandbox).

comparisons.difference: A similar tree of accounts. AWS SCPs limit permissions; Azure management groups carry RBAC and Policy assignments that pass down.
Resource groups hold resources in one subscription and can't nest. Management groups hold subscriptions and can nest six levels deep.

misconceptions.myth: A subscription can be in several management groups.
misconceptions.reality: No. Each subscription has exactly one parent.
No. They hold only management groups and subscriptions.
No. Resources keep running. Only the inherited rules and roles change.

architectureDecisions: Keep the tree shallow: 3 or 4 levels, built around rules (platform, landing zones, sandbox), not the company org chart.
Broad rules high, specific rules low: put company-wide rules near the top and team-specific ones further down.
Control new subscriptions: set a default management group that has rules, and require permission to create management groups.

walkthrough.subtitle: Govern many subscriptions at once by placing them in a tree.

steps.label: Many subscriptions
steps.title: Twenty subscriptions, twenty copies of every rule
body: Each team has its own subscription. Assigning the same policy and the same roles twenty times is slow and error-prone.

steps.label: The tree
steps.title: Management groups form a tree above subscriptions
body: A management group holds subscriptions and other management groups, up to six levels deep (not counting the root). The top is the tenant root group, created automatically.

steps.label: Inherit
steps.title: Assign once, apply everywhere below
body: Policies and role assignments at a management group flow down to every subscription, resource group and resource under it.

steps.label: Limits
steps.title: Rules of the tree
body: Up to 10,000 management groups per tenant. Each subscription or management group has exactly one parent. Moving a subscription needs rights on the subscription and on the target group.
To manage the root, a Global Administrator can elevate access (Entra ID > Properties > Access management for Azure resources).

handsOn.title: Create a management group and place your subscription in it
before: Signed in at portal.azure.com as Owner of a subscription (a free or pay-as-you-go account works). Work in a resource group called rg-az104-lab.
Your account must be able to manage management groups. In a personal tenant you are Global Administrator; if you get an authorization error, see the tip in step 1.

steps.do: Search 'Management groups'. If asked, select 'Start using management groups'.
steps.see: The Tenant Root Group with your subscription under it.
steps.tip: Authorization error? Open Microsoft Entra ID > Properties, set 'Access management for Azure resources' to Yes, Save, sign out and in. Turn it back to No at the end.

steps.do: Select + Create. ID: mg-lab, display name: Lab. Submit.
steps.see: mg-lab under the Tenant Root Group (refresh after a minute).

steps.do: Open mg-lab > + Add subscription, choose your subscription. Save.
steps.see: Your subscription now listed under mg-lab.

steps.do: Open mg-lab > Access control (IAM) > Add role assignment: Reader for Ana Lab (from the identity labs).
steps.see: A role assignment at the management group scope.

steps.do: Open your subscription > Access control (IAM) > Role assignments.
steps.see: Ana's Reader assignment shown as inherited from mg-lab (scope: management group).

check: Ana's role on the subscription shows as inherited from mg-lab.
cleanup: Move the subscription back to the Tenant Root Group, then delete mg-lab.
If you elevated access, set it back to No.
